question: to the Commission Barbara Bonte (PfE) Subject:

According to recent reports by Prisoners Defenders, the Cuban regime systematically subjects political prisoners to harsh forced labour conditions without any legal protection.1 In prisons such as Quivicán, prisoners work up to 15 hours a day rolling cigars by hand. The Cuban state-owned company Tabacuba itself acknowledged the use of prisoners in cigar production. Regulation (EU) 2024/3015 on forced labour prohibits imports into the European Union of products made by forced labour as of 14 December 2027. 1.
Is the Commission aware of the systematic use of political prisoners in the manufacture of products under forced labour?

Is the Commission considering suspending the Political Dialogue and Cooperation Agreement with Cuba as long as the regime continues to exploit political prisoners for the production of export goods destined for the European market?
Does the Commission consider the use of political prisoners to produce these products, under forced labour, to be a violation of Regulation (EU) 2024/2015 on forced labour?
https://hrwf.eu/cubas-prison-business-60000-prisoners-are-used-as-slave-labor/.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.7.2026) As recalled during the intervention of the High Representative/Vice President at the plenary of the European Parliament on 19 May 2026, Cuba urgently needs to make fundamental political, economic and democratic reforms, respecting the human rights and fundamental freedoms of the Cuban people and releasing political prisoners and all individuals who have been arbitrarily detained. The EU, including through its Delegation in Havana and its Special Representative for Human Rights, regularly raises cases of political prisoners with the Cuban authorities. The Political Dialogue and Cooperation Agreement with Cuba1 establishes a framework for the EU to engage with Cuban authorities, including in areas of divergence such as the detention of political prisoners. Regarding forced labour, the Commission follows closely information about the presence of forced labour in Cuba, including through reports from international organisations, civil society and other relevant stakeholders and takes the allegations very seriously. From the entry into application of Regulation (EU) 2024/3015 in December 20272, the Commission and competent authorities of Member States will be able to investigate products suspected to be made with forced labour, included on the basis of submissions of information made by stakeholders.
